comparison.reading: gradient_boosting is ahead of random_forest by 0.0171 of curve area. That gap holds in every re-draw, but it is above the 0.005 we fixed in advance as the smallest difference worth acting on. With 1,044,467 flights a tiny gap can be perfectly repeatable and still not matter.

examples.kind: Confident misses — late, scored as low risk
Confident false alarms — on time, scored as high risk

secondary_check.design: Fitted on months [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9] and scored on the held-out flights from months [11, 12].
secondary_check.reading: 1.20 times the base rate, against 1.87 on the main split. Two things make this harder and they are tangled together: the later months are a different period from the ones the model was fitted on, and their month values are outside the range it ever saw, so it has to extrapolate. That is exactly why the main split draws held-out days from every month instead.

provenance: Models and settings were chosen in p3 by cross-validation on training days only. The decision threshold came from the same folds. p4 refitted the chosen settings on every training row. This script read test.csv once and measured; it fitted nothing except the clearly-labelled secondary check, and re-tuned nothing.
